title: Peter Explains His Actions, The Church in Antioch

questions.question: When Peter returned to Jerusalem, who criticized him for going to uncircumcised men and eating with them?
options: The circumcision party
The Pharisees in the church
The elders of the Jerusalem church
The twelve apostles themselves
questions.explanation: Acts 11:2-3 (ESV): "So when Peter went up to Jerusalem, the circumcision party criticized him, saying, 'You went to uncircumcised men and ate with them.'"

questions.question: As Peter recounted the story, he said the Holy Spirit fell on Cornelius's household "just as on us at the beginning." Then he remembered the word of the Lord. What specific thing had the Lord said?
options: "John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit."
"The Spirit will be poured out on all flesh."
"Go into all the world and preach to every creature."
"You will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes."
questions.correctAnswer: "John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit."
questions.explanation: Acts 11:16 (ESV): "And I remembered the word of the Lord, how he said, 'John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.'"

questions.question: After Peter's explanation, the circumcision party fell silent. What was their conclusion?
options: "Then to the Gentiles also God has granted repentance that leads to life."
"This must be the work of the Spirit and we cannot oppose God."
"We will bring this matter before the council for a final decision."
"Peter is correct; circumcision is no longer required for salvation."
questions.correctAnswer: "Then to the Gentiles also God has granted repentance that leads to life."
questions.explanation: Acts 11:18 (ESV): "When they heard these things they fell silent. And they glorified God, saying, 'Then to the Gentiles also God has granted repentance that leads to life.'"

questions.question: The scattered believers initially preached only to Jews. But some men from Cyprus and Cyrene went to Antioch and spoke to whom?
options: Greeks also, preaching the Lord Jesus
Samaritans, bringing them the word of God
Egyptians in Alexandria, proclaiming the resurrection
Romans in the garrison, testifying of Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: Greeks also, preaching the Lord Jesus
questions.explanation: Acts 11:20 (ESV): "But there were some of them, men of Cyprus and Cyrene, who on coming to Antioch spoke to the Hellenists also, preaching the Lord Jesus."

questions.question: The Jerusalem church sent Barnabas to Antioch. When he arrived and saw the grace of God, what did he do?
options: He was glad, and he exhorted them all to remain faithful to the Lord with steadfast purpose
He immediately organized them into elders, deacons, and teachers
He reported back to Jerusalem before taking any action
He rebuked some who were not following the Law of Moses
questions.correctAnswer: He was glad, and he exhorted them all to remain faithful to the Lord with steadfast purpose
questions.explanation: Acts 11:23 (ESV): "When he came and saw the grace of God, he was glad, and he exhorted them all to remain faithful to the Lord with steadfast purpose of heart,"

questions.question: After Barnabas's work at Antioch, he went to Tarsus to look for whom?
options: Saul
Peter
Timothy
Philip
questions.explanation: Acts 11:25 (ESV): "So Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul,"

questions.question: For how long did Barnabas and Saul meet with the church at Antioch, teaching a great many people?
options: A whole year
Six months
Three months
Two years
questions.explanation: Acts 11:26 (ESV): "For a whole year they met with the church and taught a great many people."

questions.question: In Antioch the disciples were called something for the first time. What were they called?
options: Christians
Followers of the Way
Nazarenes
Brethren
questions.explanation: Acts 11:26 (ESV): "And in Antioch the disciples were first called Christians."

questions.question: Prophets came from Jerusalem to Antioch. One named Agabus stood up and foretold what?
options: A great famine over all the world (which came to pass under Claudius)
A great persecution coming for the church in Jerusalem
Paul would be arrested and bound in the holy city
A great earthquake would strike Jerusalem and Judea
questions.correctAnswer: A great famine over all the world (which came to pass under Claudius)
questions.explanation: Acts 11:28 (ESV): "And one of them named Agabus stood up and foretold by the Spirit that there would be a great famine over all the world (this took place in the days of Claudius)."

questions.question: How did the Antioch disciples respond to the prophecy of famine?
options: Every one of them determined to send relief to the brothers living in Judea, each according to his ability
They gathered and prayed for three days for the famine to be averted
They gathered an offering and gave it to the traveling prophets
They stored up provisions in Antioch for the coming crisis
questions.correctAnswer: Every one of them determined to send relief to the brothers living in Judea, each according to his ability
questions.explanation: Acts 11:29 (ESV): "So the disciples determined, everyone according to his ability, to send relief to the brothers living in Judea."

questions.question: Who delivered the relief from Antioch to the elders in Judea?
options: Barnabas and Saul
Philip and Agabus
Silas and Barnabas
Peter and John
questions.explanation: Acts 11:30 (ESV): "And they did so, sending it to the elders by the hand of Barnabas and Saul."

questions.question: Barnabas is described in Acts 11 with several characteristics. Which of these is mentioned?
options: He was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith
He was a powerful orator and skilled debater
He was a Levite who had served in the temple
He was the eldest of all the apostles in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: He was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith
questions.explanation: Acts 11:24 (ESV): "for he was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith. And a great many people were added to the Lord."

questions.question: Peter recounted to the Jerusalem church that a voice told him to not call what "common"?
options: What God has cleansed
Those whom God has accepted
Food permitted by the new covenant
Gentile peoples who seek after God
questions.explanation: Acts 11:9 (ESV): "But the voice answered a second time from heaven, 'What God has cleansed, do not call common.'"

questions.question: Peter described his vision in Joppa. He said the sheet contained four kinds of creatures. Which of the following is NOT in the list?
options: Fish of the sea
Four-footed animals
Reptiles
Birds of the air
questions.explanation: Acts 11:6 (ESV): "Looking at it closely, I observed animals and beasts of prey and reptiles and birds of the air." Fish are not mentioned in Peter's retelling here.

questions.question: The Spirit told Peter to go with the men from Cornelius "making no distinction." How many men did Cornelius send to Peter?
options: Three men
Two men
Six men
Twelve men
questions.explanation: Acts 11:11 (ESV): "And behold, at that very moment three men arrived at the house in which we were, sent to me from Caesarea."

key_verse_text: And in Antioch the disciples were first called Christians.
